#3055. You Could Learn to Pilot This ‘Flying Car’ in Just 5 Minutes

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Is it a bird? Is it a plane? Is it a... flying Cybertruck? Nope, it's a modular flying machine that will take to the skies next year.

When I first laid eyes on the Aridge flying car at the IFA consumer electronics show in Berlin this past September, I didn’t fully understand what I was looking at.

Taking pride of place on the stand belonging to Chinese robotics company Xpeng, there was a van that bore more than a passing resemblance to a Cybertruck. It didn’t have any wings, and it looked far too dense to fly. Sitting next to it was a kind of oversized drone with a cabin just about large enough to fit two people.

The two vehicles seemed like totally separate entities. It never would’ve occurred to me to assume they were two halves of one system – much less that the drone, with its substantial wingspan, could fold up to fit inside the van.

I now understand that this modular two-part flying car system is known formally as the Aridge Land Aircraft Carrier. The ground vehicle, also known as the mothership, is a chunky 5.5-meter-long van that can be driven with a standard license and fits in most parking spaces. It’s designed to store, carry and deploy the electric vertical takeoff and landing vehicle, or eVTOL, including its six foldable rotors, which can fly as high as a helicopter for 30km (about 19 miles).

This remarkable creation is the work of Deli Zhao, founder and president of Aridge, which is backed by robotics and auto company Xpeng. Speaking at Web Summit in Lisbon on Tuesday, Zhao presented himself as a man who was inspired to pursue a career building flying cars by Harry Potter and the Green Goblin, despite his lack of formal education.

“Dreams are very important,” Zhao said, as a video of him flying the eVTOL played on a screen in the background. Anyone can learn to fly the vehicle with just five minutes of training, he added. Or if you’re too tired to use the simple joystick, the eVTOL can fly itself autonomously.

“Everyone here can be a pilot,” Zhao said. “Everyone can be a captain.”

This sounds like a story from the very kinds of science fiction that sparked the creation of the Land Aircraft Carrier in the first place – and yet, it isn’t. It’s far from the first time I’ve seen a flying car concept at a tech event. They’ve been showing up for almost a decade at this point. But what marks this one apart is that Xpeng says it has already taken 17,000 orders for the vehicle across China, the UAE and other Asian markets.

“Our advantage is we’re closer to commercialization,” Zhao said. Xpeng has established the world’s first mass-production factory for flying cars in Guangzhou, with trial production beginning in November last year. Right now, it’s ramping up capacity and improving quality with the aim of eventually being able to build a flying car in 30 minutes.

Aridge has worked through many different concepts, including flying motorcycles, to finally find one ready for commercial production (plus it has a six-seater air taxi and integrated flying car in the works for the future too). If you have $300,000 going spare, the Land Aircraft Carrier could soon be yours.

The vast majority of preorders are from individuals, according to Xpeng, but the vehicle has also been designed for use in tourism and search and rescue. Zhao said it solves multiple problems with existing eVTOLs simultaneously: storage (it lives in the back of the mothership), recharging (it charges as the mothership is driving), transportation to and from appropriate flight sites, and ease of use.

“I hope to make flying accessible to everyone as soon as possible,” Zhao said. Right now, it takes around 20 to 30 hours of training to acquire the sport pilot license you’d need to fly the eVTOL. In China, Zhao said he’s in conversation with the regulator to reduce this, emphasizing his vehicle’s ease of use.

Zhao said he’s learned a lot from the aviation sector in China, where the Land Aircraft Carrier has gone through extensive safety testing and will likely take to the skies first as a consumer-owned product as soon as next summer. Growing its low-altitude economy, which encompasses drone delivery and eVTOLs, is national policy for the country – in spite of calls for more regulation after a deadly crash in Beijing this summer.

Xpeng is also eyeing the European market, although the regulatory hurdles are likely to be substantial. “Europe’s aviation sector is highly developed,” Zhao said, expressing his respect for the region’s strict rules, but adding that the market was important. The company will also start exploring certification in the US next year, he said. Actual progress will depend on the outcomes, he added.

In spite of Zhao’s boundless optimism, it’s difficult to buy into the hype around his flying car without witnessing it in action in person. I’ve now seen the Land Aircraft Carrier twice in different locations and videos of it in operation, but I want to observe the eVTOL’s deployment from the mothership and its airborne skills for myself.

At one point during his Web Summit talk, Zhao climbed into the cockpit of the eVTOL on stage. For a moment it seemed as though he might fly it right then and there inside Lisbon’s cavernous ME Arena. The audience raised their phones in unison, only to drop them again in disappointment when they realized Zhao wasn’t actually going to take off.

No matter how idiot-proof it might be to fly, it turns out European health and safety rules still apply.

Disclosure: Katie Collins traveled to Lisbon as a guest of Web Summit to serve as a panel moderator. Her reporting from the event was independent of that role.

#3054. Claude can collaborate in your team meetings soon – like an intern

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Claude is responding 'Yes' to that calendar invite - with some limitations. Plus: Anthropic launches two more new features that are available now.

Anthropic often refers to its Claude agent as your coworker. Soon, the company said, it will be able to join your meetings like one, and start working on the tasks you and your team are discussing live.

Also: I locked down my OpenClaw agent with Claude Code – then dared it to escape

“Claude Meetings will let you add Claude to a call to take notes and update the documents your team is working on during the conversation,” Anthropic said. The feature, which will be available for Team and Enterprise plans, theoretically goes beyond something like Gemini’s Google Meet transcription and note-taking, which identifies action items but doesn’t proactively contribute to them.

In material shared with ZDNET prior to the launch, the company said Claude “won’t join a call with outside guests unless an admin allows it, and it leaves if one joins anyway.” The company also said Claude Meetings will be on by default for Team plans, but Enterprise admins will be able to choose who gets it. The feature won’t work for organizations with “zero data retention (ZDR), HIPAA-ready configuration or customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).”

The company did not clarify when Meetings would roll out, but announced several other updates for companies that are available now.

To further keep as much of your work ecosystem within the Claude universe, Anthropic released a new Whiteboards feature in beta.

Also: Claude’s Record-a-Skill cut my research to minutes

“Now, you can talk through a messy plan out loud with Claude, and Claude can turn it into a board with a timeline with owners and dates, so you and your team can collaborate in real time,” Anthropic said. Claude will group crowdsourced notes into themes and action items. Maybe double-check the results of that spew before locking anything in.

After brain-dumping like you might on a physical whiteboard, Anthropic said, Claude can turn that output into a deck or document, or export it to other tools for next steps.

A new Sheets feature is exactly as it sounds: Claude can now create shareable spreadsheets from a prompt and edit inside cells with trackable changes. But it’s not fully replacing the old guard of spreadsheets just yet.

“When you need the full functionality of Excel, you can export your file to .xlsx or CSV, or use Claude for Excel,” Anthropic said. “You can also continue working in partner tools including Airtable, Asana, monday.com, and Smartsheet.”

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a free, local AI stack

Claude Dashboards, which only launched in beta last month, is now called Data. The tool can query company data from large external services such as Amazon Redshift and ClickHouse and comes with tracked changes and faster loading thanks to caching. According to Anthropic, it’s intended to let companies standardize metrics to avoid having conflicting data, surface data stories, and create a live source of truth everyone can access.

“With live sharing, your colleagues can see up-to-date numbers when they open a shared dashboard, even if they don’t have access to the connectors that keep that data current. Viewers see the results of the queries you’ve approved, and can’t run others with your access,” the company said.

Anthropic said that for Team plans, all three features are on by default. For Enterprise plans, only Claude Data will be on by default starting Nov. 19. Whiteboards and Sheets are off by default, though you can adjust those settings in Artifacts.

Anthropic has maintained a lead over OpenAI by focusing on enterprise clients first, while OpenAI has prioritized several consumer products. Releases like this are unsurprising, as they serve Anthropic’s primary base. Both Anthropic and OpenAI are increasingly branching into workplace and productivity software for large-scale companies. That said, Anthropic’s recent release of a personal finance tool rivals OpenAI’s existing equivalent geared toward consumers.

Also: Claude’s new Personal Finance tool aims to help analyze your spending

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

In September, at its Dev Day, OpenAI released ChatGPT Space, which houses document and slide creation tools reminiscent of Google Workspace. Before that, Anthropic had similarly consolidated its document and slide creation features into a single hub.

If there’s a slight differentiator here versus Google Workspace, it’s interface seamlessness. Anthropic has designed Claude itself as the starting point for a range of workplace deliverables, rather than maintaining distinct applications that can quickly feel siloed.

#3052. Fastly: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Operating leverage lets Fastly add revenue without matching hardware costs, a structural edge that matters as global traffic keeps climbing.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 4, 2026, Fastly (FSLY -3.32%) reported record quarterly revenue of $190.2 million. The edge cloud platform speeds up websites and secures network traffic, and it's expanding customer accounts while boosting operating profits. Three takeaways from management's comments stand out for long-term investors.

Fastly's shifting customers from single-product bandwidth delivery to a unified platform offering six product suites. When clients adopt multiple suites, switching costs increase and net retention rate, which measures spending expansion from existing accounts, climbs.

Artificial intelligence models rely on autonomous software agents that interact with enterprise applications. Fastly sells security tools like web application firewalls, which block online threats, to govern and protect agentic traffic and secure critical workloads.

Fastly delivers higher revenue over its software-defined infrastructure without needing matching increases in physical equipment costs. This operational leverage boosts operating income, which measures profits after operating expenses, and builds cash reserves.

Traffic demand across global networks keeps expanding, giving software-defined edge platforms a structural cost advantage over legacy networks. Management is focusing on customer acquisition beyond top accounts and strategic network partnerships to sustain momentum.

#3051. AMD Issues Fix for GPU Software Issue That Wore Down SSDs

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Computing > Computer Accessories > Components > Graphic cards

AMD released a new version of its Adrenalin Edition graphics software to address excessive SSD writing.

Machines that use AMD graphics hardware such as these Radeon 6800 cards may be affected by a bug in the company's driver software that is causing unnecessary writing to solid-state drives, which can wear them down over time.

AMD issued a software update on Thursday to fix a driver issue that caused excessive, continuous data writes to solid-state drives across its Radeon GPU lineup.

First reported on sites including Tom’s Hardware and Neowin, the bug was traced to two pieces of software: AMD External Events Client Module and Utility, known as atieclxx.exe or atiesrxx.exe under Windows processes. The background service handles monitoring functions, but as some users have noticed, it’s also writing a large amount of data to SSDs, as much as 432GB in 24 hours, according to Neowin.

The optional update is available on AMD’s website as Adrenalin Edition 26.11.1. In the notes for the update, AMD said the new software addresses “excessive system-drive writes while the system is idle on Radeon RX 7000 series graphics products and above” and “excessive system-drive writes while moving or resizing application windows.”

This excessive data writing is a concern because it can accelerate the wear and tear on an SSD, potentially shortening its lifespan. According to PC Gamer, that could mean losing 1% of the drive’s health in just a month. As one Reddit poster pointed out, this is not a new bug and, in one case, may have caused SSD degradation for nearly a year and a half.

Company staffers were previously posting on Reddit that a fix was coming.

The cost of SSDs has spiked dramatically in the last couple of years, so it could be an expensive problem to fix if it causes significant wear on a drive.

The same Reddit users who helped uncover the bug and spread the word have a few ideas for how to prevent this if you haven’t updated to the new software. First, check the Windows Resource Monitor (you can access it by pressing Windows key + R and typing “resmon”) and look in the Disk tab to see if you’re experiencing excessive writing to your SSD from either atieclxx.exe or atiesrxx.exe processes.

Some who are seeing this are disabling the External Events software entirely. You can do that in Windows by typing Windows key + R and entering “services.msc.” Once there, you can look for the AMD External Events Utility, open its Properties and set Startup Type to Disabled. That will keep it from starting up automatically when you reboot. You can also stop the process while you’re there for the current session. You’ll want to restart your computer after this change.

Keep in mind that disabling the software could affect some display functions and game performance. Others have tried disabling a Resizable Bar, or ReBAR, a PCI Express process for accessing video card memory. Some have switched to alternative AMD drivers that are only compatible with AMD chipsets, not those with Intel or other chipset motherboards.

These options may be a temporary fix if you’re unable to install the new software, but be warned: Using any of those methods carries the risk of breaking other functions on your machine, so make sure your system has a recent restore point.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

More phones are getting Gemini Intelligence, but only Pixel users can access it in a new way.

Gemini Intelligence is spreading beyond the Google Pixel 11 lineup to the Pixel 10, the upcoming Motorola Signature 27, and several of Samsung’s Galaxy foldables and flagship phones.

Though Google often offers its most upgraded features to other Android phone manufacturers, there are some features that are Pixel-exclusive or come to Pixel users first. This time, Gemini Intelligence is coming to Android Auto, but only for eligible Pixel users.

Also: I’m an Android Auto ride or die – but Apple CarPlay beats it on these 3 features

Google’s blog post states that Pixel users with Gemini Intelligence can expect it to gather information from their apps and surface it to their car’s infotainment screen. Google’s example is that if a friend texts you asking where you’re meeting for Pilates, Gemini Intelligence can find the correct confirmation email and offer to send it with one tap.

To access Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto, the Gemini app and subsequent setup are required; it’s available in select countries to users aged 18 and older, and feature availability will vary.

With more context about your messages, emails, and calendar events, a more capable assistant can complete cross-app tasks while driving, such as “remind me to buy mom a birthday card before her birthday” or “which route to my dentist appointment will be the fastest?” I often use Siri AI in CarPlay for tasks like these, and Gemini operates the same way. However, these tasks require user input first; what makes an AI assistant in in-car software great is when it suggests tasks before you ask for them.

Siri suggests to me when I should leave my house for an upcoming event in my calendar, such as a dinner reservation, flight, or doctor’s appointment, based on traffic conditions. It looks like Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto will offer the same assistance. I’ve reached out to Google to confirm, and will update this article if I get a response.

Also: 4 wireless Android Auto adapters we recommend (and they’re cheap)

I find Siri’s upgraded capabilities most useful when I have a busy day and heavy Atlanta traffic is thrown in the mix. Sometimes people need information about where to meet up, but I don’t remember the exact name of the location or which street it’s on. It’s difficult to search through my old messages or emails while staying alert to crazed drivers on the interstate, so a smarter AI assistant comes in handy.

Though Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto is reserved for Pixel users, the upgrade follows a series of improvements Google has rolled out to its in-car software. Non-Pixel Android phones and Android phones without Gemini Intelligence can use Personal Intelligence, which connects Gemini across your Google Maps, Photos, or Gmail data.

Personal Intelligence users can ask Gemini to navigate to a restaurant with a specific cuisine or vibe, or search their photos to find a car wash they photographed last week. Gemini Intelligence is more proactive and expansive, drawing on more sensitive data from your phone, such as messages, while Personal Intelligence relies solely on data from your Google services.

#3048. Is CoreWeave Stock a Buy After Its Latest Earnings?

There are good reasons to be bullish about CoreWeave stock, but the risk is real too.

CoreWeave (CRWV -6.13%) just delivered another impressive quarter. Revenue surged 168% year over year to $3.7 billion, its customer backlog reached $132.5 billion, and management raised its full-year guidance. Yet the company still reported a net loss of $709 million.

For investors, this creates an interesting dilemma. CoreWeave is becoming an increasingly important player in the AI infrastructure market, but its business requires enormous amounts of capital to grow.

I'd consider CoreWeave a speculative buying opportunity after its recent sell-off, but I wouldn't make it a large position in the portfolio just yet. Here are three things investors should consider.

The strongest part of CoreWeave's latest earnings is its revenue growth.

Quarterly revenue reached $3.7 billion, up from $1.37 billion a year earlier. More importantly, revenue increased approximately 42% sequentially from the previous quarter. Its backlog also expanded to $132.5 billion, up by 138% year over year.

These figures suggest demand for specialized AI computing infrastructure remains strong. CoreWeave is not simply benefiting from enthusiasm surrounding AI. It is winning customers and bringing infrastructure online to serve them.

Management also raised its 2026 revenue guidance to between $13 billion and $13.3 billion. This strengthens the long-term investment case. As AI models become more sophisticated and businesses deploy more AI applications, demand for computing capacity could remain substantial.

However, investors should remember that a large backlog represents future business, not guaranteed profits. CoreWeave still needs to build the infrastructure and deliver computing services before it recognizes much of that revenue.

CoreWeave generated $2.3 billion in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) during the quarter, an impressive 169% increase year over year. But its generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) operating income was only $207 million. Net interest expense reached $846 million, contributing to a quarterly net loss of $709 million.

CoreWeave must invest heavily in GPUs, data centers, and electricity to serve its customers. These assets are expensive and lose value over time. The company also borrows substantial amounts to finance its expansion.

This creates a difficult economic equation. CoreWeave needs to keep investing to capture demand, but those investments also generate depreciation and financing costs, creating future funding requirements.

The good news is that management raised its adjusted operating income guidance to between $1.275 billion and $1.375 billion. It also expects to achieve positive adjusted net income in the first half of 2028.

These are encouraging developments, but investors should focus on execution rather than projections. I'd particularly watch whether operating earnings grow faster than interest expenses and whether the company gradually narrows the gap between operating cash flow and capital expenditure.

Until then, impressive revenue growth alone isn't enough to establish that CoreWeave is an attractive investment.

Following its recent sell-off, CoreWeave's valuation has become more interesting. As of this writing, the stock has a market capitalization of around $27 billion. With an expected 2026 revenue of $13 billion to $13.3 billion, the stock trades at roughly 2 times sales.

That might look inexpensive for a company growing revenue at 168%. However, CoreWeave also carries substantial debt. Including its debt and cash position, its enterprise value will be much higher. For perspective, CoreWeave’s financial obligations – debt plus lease obligations – stand at about $67 billion. This is a more meaningful comparison for a capital-intensive business.

The opportunity is that CoreWeave could become a major AI infrastructure provider if it continues winning customers and improves its operating economics. The risk is that competition from Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet intensifies, computing prices decline, and financing costs remain elevated.

I'd therefore avoid treating the recent share-price decline as an automatic buying opportunity. It's definitely cheaper than a few months ago, but it's not a no-brainer.

CoreWeave's latest results strengthen its position as an important AI infrastructure provider. Revenue is growing rapidly, its backlog is expanding, and management is raising its expectations. But the company still has to prove that it can turn its enormous infrastructure investments into sustainable profits.

For investors comfortable with significant volatility, a small initial position could make sense. More conservative investors may prefer to wait for clearer evidence of improving profitability and cash generation before making their next move.

#3047. Google Catches Up to Apple, With Digital Wallet Keys for Your Physical Home Lock

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Google Wallet can unlock Android users' doors who have compatible smart locks.

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

Android users looking for the most high-tech ways to manage their smart locks at home just got some great news. On Tuesday, Google announced it will start offering digital keys in Google Wallet built on Aliro, a new smart lock standard.

When I tested the predictive, futuristic Schlage Sense Pro lock — which uses ultrawideband technology and Apple Home Keys in Apple Wallet — Schlage told me that other brands were adopting Aliro to bring that same seamless usability to more devices, and now the time has come.

The best thing about the lock is that it didn’t require me to tap my phone for an NFC connection or even wave it in the vicinity. The ultrawideband, or UWB tech — think of it like an advanced version of Bluetooth older locks used — sensed a key holder was coming to the door, judged my speed and trajectory based on the signals the lock was getting, and had the door unlocked by the time I reached it, with autolock features locking it back up a minute later.

Home keys in Google Wallet, which have already started rolling out to Public Preview users in Google Home, offer users a lot of similar tricks with the right smart locks. That’s handy not only for saving time fumbling for your phone at the door, but also if your hands are full or you’re busy talking to someone. When I tested Schlage’s version, it could sense when I was actually approaching and when I was simply walking by the door, too, so the lock didn’t randomly open.

So far, locks compatible with UWB and the “unlock on approach” feature include not only the Schlage Sense Pro ($394.98) I tested, but also the Aqara u400 ($269.99) and the European brand Nuki Keypad 2 NFC lock ($179), with more on the way. Aliro was only officially released early in 2026, so it will take time for the standard to be broadly adopted by both locks and digital wallets, especially more advanced abilities like these. The good news is that Aliro includes encryption for security, battery-life savings and other benefits, too.

A representative from Google didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The “unlock on approach” feature of Aliro’s standard digital wallet keys is only one of the advantages of this upgrade, so you don’t need a UWB-compatible lock to get the benefits.

According to Google, its own home keys in Google Wallet will offer NFC to tap your phone to unlock the door (no unlocking necessary), let you use the digital key across multiple locks if necessary, and sync your key across compatible devices you use. Other people in the home can add their own home keys to the Wallet, but unlike Apple’s temporary passes, Google says guests and visitors will need to get passcodes instead of digital keys of their own.

What happens if you or someone else loses their phone? In most cases, users can rely on keypad access codes to gain entry instead of the digital wallet. But these UWB locks sometimes forgo a physical key slot entirely: Schlage says its lock doesn’t have a key slot to reduce the risk of lockpicking, but that does limit emergency unlock options.

Here’s where this new lock technology gets more complicated. Finding a compatible lock is only a part of unlocking all these Wallet key features.

You’ll also need an NFC-enabled Android phone running Android 9 or later, such as the Google Pixel 10 Pro or Pixel Fold. Then you’ll need a Matter-enabled Google Hub with a Thread Border Router, which is typically a separate Google device, like a Nest Hub Max, Nest Wifi Pro system or Google TV streamer.

With all that, make sure your phone, lock, Google Wallet app and Google Home app are all updated, and you should be prompted to create home keys during your lock setup. This takes only a few seconds, and you can delete them easily, just like you could with a concert ticket or credit card.

Oura's acquisition of Counsel Health could signal a new dawn for digital care.

Oura has entered into an agreement to acquire AI primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The acquisition of Counsel Health, which was already a partner in the Oura app, will give users access to Counsel’s in-house physicians and 24/7 medical AI.

The Oura Ring has evolved from its beginnings as a sleep tracker to what its CEO, Tom Hale, calls “a doctor in your pocket.” The company has its sights set on making the device a continuous medical companion, and Counsel’s acquisition is one way it’s furthering that mission.

Oura employs its 24/7 health monitoring to recognize potential deviations from a user’s biometric baseline, and the partnership will build on those capabilities by adding more clinical guidance through Counsel Health.

The partnership will also connect members with Counsel Health’s medical AI and in-house physicians to address timely health problems, support, or “prescriptions for episodic health conditions,” the press release said. The acquisition offers specialty and chronic care for chronic conditions, like reproductive, aging, and cardiometabolic-related conditions.

“Oura tells members what’s happening in their bodies, and Counsel helps them act on it. This combination expands our addressable market and deepens the value we deliver to every member,” David Shuman, executive chairman of Oura, said in a press release.

This is the third acquisition Oura has made this year, following its acquisition of Galen AI, a conversational and personal health platform that connects smart ring data to medical records, and Doublepoint AI, an AI‑driven, biometric and gesture recognition company that could add voice or gesture controls to Oura’s next smart ring.

Also: Before you buy a smart ring, consider what you’re giving up

The Counsel Health deal is expected to close by the end of the year. It’s unknown whether access to Counsel Health physicians or the 24/7 medical AI will be included in an Oura app subscription.

Tech companies have a growing appetite for health tech startups. Last year, Samsung announced a similar acquisition of Xealth, a care platform that connects more than 500 hospitals with 70 digital health centers. The acquisition, according to Samsung VP of digital health Praveen Raja, furthers Samsung’s mission to connect the healthcare landscape, from symptom detection to care provider connection.

One of the Oura Ring’s superpowers is its ability to detect developing illnesses or deviations from my biometric baseline (a spiked resting heart rate, a higher body temperature) before I feel those symptoms. I’ve written about how my Oura Ring detected an illness earlier this year, one day before I began to feel sick.

Also: I should’ve listened to my Oura Ring when it warned me about my health

When Oura has flagged these concerns to me, I take them seriously, even as my care provider — to whom I show this data — may shrug them off. The Counsel Health acquisition enables medical AI and in-house physicians to contextualize your biometrics when you are sick or managing a chronic condition.

Will this acquisition help ease the demand for urgent care clinics? As a regular visitor to and hater of my Brooklyn CityMD, I hope so. It is notoriously difficult to get a same-day, in-person appointment with a primary care provider in New York because of high demand and a stretched-thin healthcare system, which often leaves urgent care as the only in-person option for patients.

The press release says that users could ask physicians for prescriptions. I’m thinking that if I get another bad cold this winter, I could go to my Oura app for help and symptom management instead of CityMD. Making a physician readily available to Oura users could, in theory, reduce dependence on primary or urgent care providers.

There’s a similar tension to be found in Netflix’s “The Diplomat,” where Keri Russell’s strong-willed and sharp-minded Kate Wyler must juggle her professional ambitions as the U.S. Ambassador to the U.K. with her personal duties to her husband Hal (Rufus Sewell), who, by the fourth season of the political drama, ascends to the Vice Presidency of the United States.

There might not be “Black Doves”-style spy antics in “The Diplomat,” but the fast-paced series is packed with political subterfuge, back-channel backstabbing and international intrigue. Tom’s Guide’s Kelly Woo praised the show’s most recent edition as “its best season yet”: “Season 4 doubles down on what has always made the show so much fun: putting brilliant, deeply complicated people in rooms together and watching them try to outmaneuver one another while barely holding their personal lives together,” writes Woo.

#3044. 5 Dividend Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever

These five stocks have proven track records of dividend growth backed by attractive businesses.

Johnson & Johnson (JNJ +0.79%), Procter & Gamble (PG +1.05%), and Federal Realty (FRT +0.35%) are all Dividend Kings, with at least 50 annual dividend increases. Medtronic (MDT +1.85%) is closing in on 50, while Realty Income (O -0.74%) has the shortest dividend streak at a still impressive 32 years. If you are looking for a dividend stock, this quintet is among the most reliable.

But that alone isn't enough to make them buy and hold dividend investments. What tips the scale is the fact that all five are very well-run businesses. Here's a look at each of them and why even the most conservative investor should feel comfortable jumping aboard.

The big story behind J&J and Medtronic is that they are healthcare companies. Healthcare spending tends to be resilient because of the potentially dire consequences of failing to take care of yourself. Johnson & Johnson, the Dividend King, is more diverse, with large divisions in the pharmaceutical and medical device spaces. It has the longest dividend streak of any healthcare stock. Medtronic, which has increased its dividend annually for 48 years (two shy of Dividend King status), is focused on medical devices.

Johnson & Johnson's is performing fairly well right now as a business and offers a yield of 1.9%. That's still notably above the broader market's roughly 1% yield, but the stock is best suited to risk-averse investors. Notably, it slightly increased its full-year 2026 guidance when it reported third-quarter earnings.

Medtronic is emerging from a business revamp, with growth accelerating after a period of weakness. Investors are still operating with a show-me attitude, leaving the stock with a 2.8% yield. But the medical device maker reported top-line growth of 13.7% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, prompting it to raise its full-year guidance after just one quarter. If you can handle just a little more uncertainty, most dividend investors will likely find it attractive as it continues to deliver on its turnaround promises.

Procter & Gamble is a consumer staples giant with global reach and a portfolio that includes paper products, makeup/skincare, toiletries, and over-the-counter drugs, among other things. However, the key defining factor here is that P&G products tend to sit at the high end of the market. That would suggest that it faces a material trade-down risk, but that hasn't panned out even as budget-conscious consumers pull back on spending today. The company's first quarter fiscal 2027 organic sales rose a very healthy 4%.

The key is that innovation has long driven the company's business. It leads the industry by introducing products that are worth buying despite a higher price tag. And its status as a Dividend King highlights just how successful this business approach has been. With a 2.6% yield, even the most conservative investor should feel comfortable buying P&G and socking it away for decades.

Federal Realty is the only real estate investment trust (REIT) on the Dividend King list. Realty Income, which trademarked the nickname "The Monthly Dividend Company", has 32 annual increases behind it, which is hard to complain about. Both are kind of boring businesses, which is really what you want from a REIT.

Federal Realty's yield is hovering around 4%. It owns a focused portfolio of roughly 100 large and well-located strip mall and mixed-use assets. Basically, it owns properties that retailers want to be in. And it works very hard to develop and redevelop its assets to ensure they remain desirable for tenants and shoppers. It is the type of dividend stock you buy and only check in on a couple of times a year.

Realty Income is the largest net lease REIT, with a globally diversified portfolio of over 15,500 properties. Net leases require the tenant to pay for most property-level costs, which materially reduces Realty Income's expenses and risk. To be fair, this 5.5% yielding REIT isn't going to wow you with growth; it's too big for that. But it is built from the ground up to pay reliable dividends, and its growing business diversification should support years of dividend growth. It can provide a high-yield foundation for a passive income portfolio, allowing you to buy lower-yielding but higher-growth stocks like J&J, Medtronic, and P&G.

Johnson & Johnson, Medtronic, P&G, Federal Realty, and Realty Income aren't "get rich quick" stocks. They are the types of investments you buy and hold for decades, perhaps even forever. If you are looking to generate a reliable income stream while benefiting from the long-term growth of the companies you own, this quintet should be high up on your wish list, if not on your buy list.

#3043. Google Fi now switches between the best mobile networks automatically – how it works

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Networking > Mobile Carriers

Pixel users also get a bonus Wi-Fi upgrade. Here's what to know.

From left to right: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8, Google Pixel 11, Google Pixel 11 Pro XL.

Google Fi wireless customers with Pixel phones just got a serious upgrade to their mobile and Wi-Fi connections for free.

Google has announced two new “super network” connection features for Fi Wireless: one that automatically switches between two of the largest 5G cellular networks, and another that automatically connects to premium Wi-Fi in millions of locations without you needing to log in.

The features are rolling out today for Pixel 9 phones and newer models on every Google Fi plan. If you’re not a current Fi customer, you can sign up for a free seven-day trial to test it alongside your current carrier.

Here’s how the new mobile connection feature works: if your main connection slows or becomes unstable, Fi will automatically move to a secondary connection. This not only means you’ll have the fastest option when your connection is good, but you’ll have fewer dead zones when service is limited.

Also: I compared Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T 5G coverage on a road trip – and the winner surprised me

The feature will run on MEP (Multiple Enabled Profiles) technology, which allows a single eSIM chip to host and run multiple SIM profiles simultaneously. Footnotes in Google’s release note that you’ll need to have “any non-Fi SIMs disabled.”

Google Fi originally offered automatic switching between two networks when the service debuted a decade ago, but it was between Sprint and T-Mobile, which merged in 2020. Google didn’t reveal what the “two of America’s best 5G cellular networks” were, but ZDNET has reached out to ask. The service usually runs on T-Mobile. Along with T-Mobile, the three biggest carriers are AT&T and Verizon, so it’s likely the second carrier is one of those.

In addition to a mobile connection upgrade, users are getting better Wi-Fi, too. Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ will automatically connect you to faster Wi-Fi in millions of locations like airports and malls (Google defines “faster” as two times better reliability and 30% improved latency compared to normal Google Fi cellular networks) without you having to log in or head to your settings. These connections will be automatically encrypted, Google said, keeping your online activity safe.

Also: 6 default Pixel 11 settings I changed that made a big difference – and why

This feature is also coming to Samsung phones running One UI 9 or higher and select modern Motorola phones.

Both of these features, Google explained, are available internationally and are included on Unlimited Premium and Flexible plans at no extra cost.

#3042. After Jensen Huang, Big Tech Has a Chance to Learn From Nvidia’s Mistakes

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech insiders and commentators say Nvidia will survive Huang's departure, but it's time for more accountability among CEOs.

What now for Nvidia? This was the question on everyone’s lips at the illustrious Web Summit technology conference in Lisbon on Thursday in the hours after CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation.

Huang’s departure followed a series of allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an Nvidia employee and one with a woman who has been identified as a possible Chinese spy. The company, whose computer chips are at the core of generative AI’s disruptive powers, is valued at around $4 trillion, making it one of the most valuable in the world. A co-founder, Huang has been with Nvidia since its earliest days three decades ago, making it hard to imagine the company without him at the helm.

There’s nothing quite like a salacious, market-moving scandal to create a buzz at a tech event. The Web Summit organizers leaned into the news, quickly assembling a panel of tech experts to discuss whether Nvidia was bigger than its CEO.

Nothing in the allegations changes the fact that Huang is probably the godfather of the AI revolution, said investor and financial writer Adam Kobeissi. “He was the central figure,” Kobeissi said, even if he wasn’t the only person responsible for Nvidia’s success.

“This company is going to survive and thrive with or without him,” he added. “I don’t think this is some sort of bubble-popping moment where everything comes crumbling down.”

Sweeping financial investments and expectations across the AI industry have driven stock prices and company valuations to dizzying heights, with many critics warning of a bubble just waiting to burst with destabilizing effects. As powerful as Nvidia has become, it could be caught in the center of such a maelstrom.

While such a concentration of power is not the way to create resilient companies, said Ryan LaSalle, CEO of cybersecurity company Nisos, like Kobeissi he thinks Nvidia will weather the storm.

Interim Nvidia CEO Collette Kress, who has been with the company since 2013, is known for having a ton of loyalty within Nvidia, he said. “In a company of that much brainpower, there will be some natural leaders who can help shepherd them to the next chapter.”

One big question put to panel participants was whether Nvidia’s board made a mistake allowing one person to have so much power.

It wasn’t just a mistake of corporate culture, said Carissa Veliz, associate professor of philosophy at the Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI. It was also a mistake in terms of democracy.

For one person to wield so much power over decisions affecting the economy and national security means something has gone wrong and has revealed how vulnerable we are, Veliz said. If we look at the history of corporations, she said, there used to be a tradition of proving to the government that you were doing good for your country to earn your right to exist and get certain tax breaks.

“At the moment, we have shifted from that kind of framework to a framework in which a corporation is allowed to be essentially a kind of psychopath that only cares about its own profits, that only has duties to shareholders and which can be structured in any way, including a very powerful CEO with very little oversight,” she said.

Gil Duran, author of The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, said that he thought Nvidia’s errors in the lead-up to this moment would be studied in business and public relations crisis management classes.

“The board was completely missing out on most of the truth and the facts,” he said, referencing news reports that said Huang a year ago hired a law firm known for covering up sex scandals and President Donald Trump in May had been told about the CEO’s affair with the alleged Chinese spy.

“I don’t think there’s any other way to look at it but a catastrophe,” he said.

Duran and Veliz agreed that it was time to ensure tech CEOs face real oversight.

“These guys face no accountability and no supervision, and that’s part of the problem,” said Veliz. “These kind of small kings have their own small kingdoms… and they get away with almost anything.”

CEOs like Elon Musk at SpaceX and Sam Altman at OpenAI have enormous influence not only in their own companies but also across the national economy.

What we’re seeing in Huang’s downfall is the shattering of a myth about genius founders, said Duran. He questioned whether it would spark actual change, however, given that the market’s addiction to the narrative of great, powerful founders.

“The fact that they can just tumble markets with their personal lives that become geopolitical crises – this is an insane amount of power to outsource,” he said.

If we can tone down the myth, this moment provides a chance to look at where we’ve gone wrong and do better, Veliz said. There’s opportunity here, she added – to raise up companies that can build the kinds of technology we need, support democracies rather than erode them, aren’t based on surveillance and prediction, and can behave transparently.

For every other tech behemoth out there, there is plenty to be learned from Huang’s downfall. The concentration of power in one individual is not, as LaSalle pointed out, a safe long-term strategy.

What’s needed is more oversight and accountability from a company’s board of directors. In announcing Huang’s resignation, Nvidia also said it was appointing its first chairman for its board.

Huang’s entanglement with a potential honeypot is also an opportunity for tech companies to think about security, said LaSalle. No matter how sophisticated cybersecurity threats are becoming in the age of AI, he added, “people are still the simplest way in.”

Duran warned about the potential damage ahead if we fail to seize this as a moment to change. “If you look at the AI CEO vision of the future, it’s massive economic destruction so that a handful of people can become trillionaires,” he said. “No one voted for that. Nobody wants that, and we have a short window of time to collapse it before they collapse us.”

Disclosure: Katie Collins traveled to Lisbon as a guest of Web Summit to serve as a panel moderator. Her reporting from the event was independent of that role.

Including House of M, chaos magic and Latverian Witches

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Scarlet Witch might have one of the most interesting roles to play in “Avengers: Doomsday,” and I’m not just saying that because Wanda Maximoff is one of my favorite Marvel characters. After seemingly meeting her end in “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness,” fans have been waiting to find out whether Elizabeth Olsen will return to the MCU. Now, with Doctor Doom seemingly taking an interest in Wanda and her extraordinary powers, there’s plenty of room for speculation about what Marvel has planned.

But why would Doom need Scarlet Witch in the first place? Wanda is one of the most powerful magic users in the Marvel universe, with reality-altering abilities that could make her an incredibly valuable ally or a terrifying enemy. Her comic-book history also offers some intriguing possibilities, particularly when you look at storylines like “House of M” and “The Children’s Crusade.”

Of course, Marvel hasn’t confirmed exactly how Wanda fits into “Avengers: Doomsday,” so we’ll have to wait and see how much of this speculation holds up. Still, there are several fascinating directions the studio could take her story. Here are five Scarlet Witch theories that could explain Doctor Doom’s interest in Wanda and what her potential MCU comeback might look like.

One popular theory is that “Avengers: Doomsday” could take inspiration from Marvel Comics’ “The Children’s Crusade.” In the comic, Wanda disappears after the events of “Avengers Disassembled” and “House of M.” Her sons, Billy and Tommy, eventually set out to find her with the Young Avengers. They discover that Wanda is living in Latveria with Doctor Doom, having lost her memories. Doom is secretly using her powerful magic for his own purposes. The young heroes eventually confront him and help Wanda escape, revealing that she has been manipulated rather than acting as a villain herself.

There are a few reasons this storyline could work in the MCU. At the end of “VisionQuest,” Vision, Billy and Tommy are together, leaving Wanda as the missing member of the family. One possibility is that Doom could erase Wanda’s memories or take advantage of her vulnerability to control her powers.

He might even use her desire to reunite with her family to keep her on his side. Of course, Marvel hasn't confirmed that it’s adapting this storyline, and we don’t yet know how much of the comic could make it into the movie. It’s also possible that Wanda’s reunion with her children will be saved for “Avengers: Secret Wars” instead.

Scarlet Witch could be connected to a mysterious group of masked characters known as the “Latverian Witches.” These figures have appeared in “Avengers: Doomsday” promotional material, including posters, convention displays and leaked concept art. One particular poster caught fans’ attention because one of the masked witches is red. This has led to speculation that Scarlet Witch could be part of the group, possibly working alongside Doctor Doom.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

There have also been reports of a “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness” page on Disney+ featuring promotional artwork showing Wanda and Doctor Strange in front of a Latverian mural. However, the details surrounding the witches are still unclear. Some reports describe three masked figures wearing different colored robes, while others point to artwork featuring four characters. There is no official confirmation that Wanda is one of them.

This theory also fits with the idea that Doom is gathering powerful characters to help carry out his plans. In the post-credits scene attached to the “Avengers: Endgame” theatrical rerelease, Doom approaches Bruce Banner in an underground bunker and tells him, “I've come to collect you.” Banner then disappears alongside Doom, leaving behind a glowing green symbol. We know he’s also collected Scarlet Witch, meaning these “witches” might all hold a special power to help Doom complete his plans.

It’s possible that Scarlet Witch could take the place of Molecule Man in Marvel’s “Secret Wars” storyline. In the comics, Doctor Doom uses enormous amounts of power to reshape reality and create Battleworld, a world made from the remains of destroyed universes. He then rules over it as God Emperor Doom.

Some fans think Marvel could use Wanda instead of introducing Molecule Man, especially since she’s already an established character with incredible reality-warping abilities. We’ve seen her create an entire town in “WandaVision” and travel between universes in “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.” That makes her a believable target for Doom, particularly after his apparent promise that her power will be his.

But how would he use it? One possibility is that Doom steals Wanda’s chaos magic to build Battleworld and take control of the multiverse. This could also connect to the Darkhold prophecy mentioned in “Agatha All Along,” which claims that the Scarlet Witch is destined to destroy the world.

There’s another possibility, though. Rather than simply forcing Wanda to help him, Doom could offer her a deal. He might promise to create a new reality where she can live happily with Vision, Billy and Tommy in exchange for her help. That would give Wanda a personal reason to side with him, even if she doesn’t fully understand his plans. It could also set up a heartbreaking conflict when her family discovers what Doom has done.

One of the biggest theories following “VisionQuest” is that Doctor Doom could use Wanda to destroy Earth-10005, the universe home to the original Fox “X-Men” movies. “Avengers: Doomsday” is expected to bring together heroes from three different universes: the MCU’s Earth-616, the Fantastic Four’s Earth-828 and the X-Men’s Earth-10005. With Marvel planning to introduce its own version of the X-Men after this saga, some fans believe the Fox universe could be destroyed as part of the story.

This theory has an interesting connection to House of M, one of Scarlet Witch’s most famous comic-book storylines. In it, Wanda utters the iconic line “No more mutants,” causing mutants to lose their powers. Elizabeth Olsen has previously said she would love to deliver the line in the MCU, but there’s been no opportunity yet. Having Wanda use her powers against the Fox “X-Men” universe could be Marvel’s way of bringing that moment to life.

It’s possible that the Sentinels shown in the “Doomsday” trailer might actually be designed to contain Wanda rather than hunt mutants. There’s also a less villainous possibility. Instead of Wanda destroying the mutants, she could turn against Doom and use her powers to stop him from wiping them out. This could lead to a twist on her famous comic-book line: “No, more mutants.” It might even set up the arrival of mutants in the rebooted MCU.

As we know in the “VisionQuest” finale, the post-credit scene revisits Wanda’s apparent death beneath Mount Wundagore in “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness,” but this time we see what happened after the temple collapsed. Doctor Doom uses green magic to lift the rubble before telling Wanda, “Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine.” Moments later, her eyes open.

But how exactly did Doom bring her back? One popular fan theory says Wanda never actually died. Instead, the red flash of magic seen as Wundagore collapsed could have been her Chaos Magic protecting her and placing her in some kind of healing coma. Doom may simply have found her and awakened her. Another possibility is that Doom rescued Wanda immediately after the collapse but kept her hidden for years. This would explain why nobody else managed to find her and why she was considered gone. Some fans even believe he could have used time travel to return to the moment Wundagore fell and save her.

There’s also the possibility that Wanda really did die and Doom used magic to resurrect her. In fact, he could have stolen power from Franklin Richards, who demonstrated the ability to bring someone back to life in “The Fantastic Four: First Steps.” Whatever the explanation, Doom clearly has a reason for bringing Wanda back, and his warning that her power will be his suggests she’s central to his plans, and could be the most powerful weapon against the Avengers.

#3039. American Express vs. S&P Global: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Two payments and data giants, one a premium card network and the other a gatekeeper of ratings and benchmarks, offer very different paths to growth and risk.

American Express (AXP +0.80%) and S&P Global (SPGI +1.08%) serve as critical infrastructure for the global economy. Choosing between the premium payments leader and the dominant data giant requires balancing consumer credit trends against capital market activity.

These companies represent two distinct corners of the market. One relies on credit demand and high-end consumer spending, while the other functions as a gatekeeper of financial intelligence. We compare these businesses to determine which model offers a more compelling path for investors.

American Express operates a unique "closed-loop" network, acting as both the card issuer and the payment processor for its transactions. In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, the company detailed how this integrated model allows it to capture revenue from both cardholder fees and merchant discounts. Its global network now spans more than 100 million merchant locations across over 200 countries and territories. The company drives growth through premium strategic partnerships with Delta Air Lines (DAL -0.35%) and Marriott International (MAR -0.35%). It also maintains relationships with Amazon(AMZN -0.29%), though it recently reclassified its small-business co-branded portfolios with that partner as held for sale. The company further streamlined its focus by exiting its investment in Global Business Travel Group in September 2026.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $72.2 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 9.5% over the prior year. This performance translated into net income of roughly $10.8 billion for the period. The company has maintained a consistent net margin of close to 15%, indicating steady profitability as it expands its international presence. High-spending cardholders provide a resilient revenue stream that often outperforms broader averages of consumer spending during economic shifts.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 1.7x. This metric measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, indicating how much the company uses borrowed funds to finance its assets. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, was nearly 0.3x. During FY 2025, the company generated roughly $16.0 billion in free cash flow, defined as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures.

S&P Global provides essential benchmarks, credit ratings, and data analytics to the global capital and commodity markets. In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, the company highlighted its role as a vital gatekeeper for asset managers, investment banks, and insurance companies. This dominant position in the fintech stocks space is supported by a global workforce of more than 40,000 employees. The company provides workflow solutions across capital, energy, and automotive markets in 43 different countries. Its diversified segments, including credit ratings and commodity insights, create a high-moat business model where customers often rely on its proprietary data for daily decision-making.

In FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $15.3 billion, an increase of nearly 7.9% from the prior year. The company reported net income of close to $4.5 billion for that period. This resulted in a strong net margin of approximately 29.2%, reflecting the highly profitable nature of selling subscription-based data and ratings. The growth in net income demonstrates the efficiency of its capital-light business model as it scales its digital offerings.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.5x. This indicates a conservative use of debt relative to shareholders' equity. The current ratio was approximately 0.8x, indicating the company's ability to cover its upcoming short-term obligations. Free cash flow for the year was close to $5.5 billion, representing the cash available for dividends and acquisitions after capital expenditures.

American Express faces intense global competition from Visa (V +1.30%) and Mastercard (MA +1.32%), along with a growing ecosystem of digital wallets and alternative payment platforms. The company also relies heavily on its partner Delta Air Lines, meaning any loss or adverse renegotiation of that relationship could harm revenue. Additional risks include regulatory scrutiny of interchange fees and heightened sensitivity to macroeconomic downturns, which could lead to higher delinquency and write-off rates across its card portfolios.

S&P Global relies heavily on complex IT infrastructure and cloud services, which create vulnerabilities to cyberattacks and data breaches that could compromise client trust. The company faces competitive pressure from both traditional data providers and new AI-driven initiatives that could offer lower-cost alternatives. Furthermore, its ratings business is highly sensitive to market volatility and debt issuance volumes, which can fluctuate significantly in response to interest rate movements and broader economic conditions.

American Express appears more affordable based on its Forward P/E, while S&P Global trades at a higher multiple, likely due to its superior net margin.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

These two stocks run on different long-term engines, and that difference matters more than any single metric. Amex grows when affluent households pay for membership, so its future depends on Millennial and Gen Z customers choosing premium cards and staying with them. Card fee growth from product refreshes shows that engine is working, and you can track it every quarter.S&P Global has a quieter engine that the credit-and-ratings story hides. Its index business earns a fee on every dollar flowing into funds that track its benchmarks, so revenue grows as more savers move to index investing, whether or not anyone issues a bond. That tailwind is why the business looks less cyclical over a decade than its ratings arm suggests.If you already own an S&P 500 index fund, you pay S&P Global fees today, and you hold a slice of its parent company inside your fund. Amex adds something that fund doesn't: a direct bet on premium spending and lending. I would buy Amex because you get a different driver and a younger customer base, which gives it years of runway. Choose S&P if you want a pure bet on the growth of passive investing.

#3038. This tiny box gives your older tech smart home superpowers – and it’s only $69

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home Assistant gets new equipment to battle planned obsolescence and abandoned cloud services.

Home Assistant is perhaps the most versatile smart home automation system of them all, thanks to the extreme customization power it offers. Today, a tiny, new box-shaped device is giving Home Assistant users a way to make their existing electronics smarter, rather than replacing them to keep up with the times.

Also: Ring’s new drone patrols your home to keep an eye on things

The Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 is a multi-purpose piece of hardware made by Nabu Casa, the company behind official Home Assistant hardware. The device brings together several connectivity options, including RS-232 serial for older TVs and other equipment, and the ability to connect older stereo systems and amplifiers to modern multi-room audio setups.

“The most sustainable device is the one you already own,” said Paulus Schoutsen, founder of Home Assistant and Nabu Casa. “No device should be left behind because it doesn’t have smart capabilities, or worst of all, its cloud services get turned off.

With the AUX-2, Home Assistant is joining the fight against planned obsolescence and abandoned cloud services.

Modern smart home systems have a major drawback: they exclude working electronics simply because they weren’t designed to integrate with today’s smart home platforms. This is the problem that the AUX-2 addresses.

Instead of buying a new stereo system with smart features, consumers can use the $69 AUX-2 to make the devices they already own smarter, more connected, and easier to control.

A single AUX-2 can control multiple devices, depending on how they’re connected and the interfaces they use. The device’s limit has more to do with the number of physical connections required.

Also: How I open-sourced my smart home – and ditched Google for Siri

The AUX-2 lets you connect two serial-controlled devices directly through the RS-232 ports. The USB port can act as an expansion for compatible adapters. You can place one AUX-2 on an entertainment center and connect an older stereo and TV, then use another AUX-2 elsewhere in your house for additional equipment with physical serial connections.

According to Home Assistant, with an AUX-2, you can control an old AV receiver without the original app, have an older TV respond to commands without relying on its manufacturer’s cloud servers, or integrate existing audio equipment into modern multiroom sound systems.

This way, consumers won’t need to trash a functional piece of equipment simply because the manufacturer stops supporting it.

Aside from RS-232 serial, the AUX-2 also supports Bluetooth, Z-Wave, USB, PoE, and Wi-Fi for connectivity.

#3037. What Is T-Mix? Navigating T-Mobile’s All-New Phone Plans and Perk Scheme

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

With a new system of "Picks," T-Mobile lets customers mix and match mobile add-ons.

T-Mobile is remixing its unlimited phone plans and introducing a structure where customers choose which services, like streaming video subscriptions or phone financing, apply to their accounts. Called T-Mix, the lineup is available now and includes four core plans that include “Picks” that can be mixed and matched every 90 days.

“T-Mobile and [other carriers] have really built a ‘good/better/best’ world” where customers choose prepackaged plans, Allan Samson, T-Mobile chief marketing officer, said during a call with CNET. “We’re going to blow that whole thing up, and you get to individually curate every experience you want.”

Much like with Verizon’s current plans, T-Mobile’s new offerings let customers pick and choose the perks they want rather than reserving some perks for certain plan tiers, as it had with its former Experience plan options. If you wanted a perk such as Hulu streaming, you had to pay up for the pricier Experience Beyond 2.0 plan. Conversely, even if you picked the Beyond plan for another reason, like unlimited mobile hotspot data, you still got Hulu whether you watched it or not.

Each of the new T-Mix plans includes a core set of high-speed data, hotspot data, video streaming speeds and international options. On top of that – and the feature that gives T-Mix its name – is a selection of Picks, which work like a type of currency to choose perks like streaming services, game passes, and services like DoorDash or T-Satellite. Picks can also go toward financing a new phone.

T-Mix replaces the existing Experience 2.0 plans for new customers, though existing customers can stay on their plans.

Despite the modular nature of Picks, T-Mobile is still sticking with its one-plan-fits-all policy for accounts with multiple lines. Unlike Verizon and AT&T, where each family member can have their own plan, everyone needs to agree on which T-Mix base to start from: Standard, More, Loaded and T-Mix Saver. The number of Picks you get depends on the plan and the number of lines on the account.

The Standard plan includes 50GB of high-speed 5G data, unlimited hotspot data at 3G speeds, unlimited international data while traveling in Canada and Mexico at 2G speeds, unlimited texting in more than 215 countries and up to 480p (SD) streaming resolution. A single line includes one Pick.

The More plan includes unlimited high-speed data, up to 60GB of high-speed hotspot data (which drops down to an unlimited amount at 3G speeds), 15GB of high-speed data in Canada and Mexico (then unlimited at 256Kbps), up to 5GB of high-speed data when traveling internationally (then unlimited at 256Kbps) and up to 4K (UHD) streaming resolution. A single line on More includes two picks.

The Loaded plan also includes unlimited high-speed data, up to 250GB of hotspot data (then unlimited at 3G speeds), 30GB of high-speed data in Canada and Mexico (then unlimited at 256Kbps), up to 15GB high-speed data when traveling (and down to 256Kbps unlimited after reaching that cap) and up to 4K (UHD) streaming resolution. On the Loaded plan, you can also connect a cellular-enabled device, such as a smartwatch or tablet, for $5 an item. A single line includes three Picks.

For those who want just basic phone service, the T-Mix Saver plan includes the same features as the Standard plan, but does not include Picks and is limited to two lines.

All plans include unlimited texting when traveling in more than 215 countries, long-distance calling at $0.50 a minute and T-Mobile’s Basic Scam Shield service.

For each plan, you can choose to finance a new phone using T-Mobile’s Standard 36-month term or the recently introduced Flex 36-month commitment that rolls in all of the upfront costs.

Pricing (with AutoPay and not including taxes and fees) for the Standard plan starts at $55 for a single line, jumps to $85 for two lines (or $42.50 a line) and then increases to $100 for three lines (or $33.33 a line). Additional lines cost $15 more apiece.

The More plan starts at $75 for one line, then goes to $130 for two lines and $155 for three lines. Additional lines add $25 each to the monthly cost.

The Loaded plan is $95 for a single line, $160 for two lines and $200 for three lines. Adding more Loaded lines costs $40 each.

The Saver plan costs $45 for a single line and $80 for two lines (the maximum number allowed). T-Mobile is currently running a promotion that brings those prices down to $30 and $65 if you switch from another provider and bring along your phone number.

An account on the first three plans can have up to 12 lines.

One advantage of T-Mobile’s now-old Experience plans was the simplicity of knowing that if you moved up to a higher tier such as Experience Beyond, you’d get a specific set of additional perks.

Picks gives you the flexibility to only activate perks you’ll actually use, but working out which to opt for is a bit complex. With Picks, there are two components at play: How many Picks you get on your account, and when you can change them. It sounds low-key chaotic on the surface, but it will start to make more sense, I promise.

T-Mobile assigns a Pick value to the perks it’s offering. For example, one Pick could get you Netflix Standard with ads or the DashPass service by DoorDash. If you want an Apple Music Individual or Google AI Pro subscription, that would use two Picks.

Higher-tier offerings such as Netflix Standard and Xbox Game Pass Ultimate are three Picks each, while Netflix Premium and ESPN Unlimited are four Picks.

Those are all services offered by T-Mobile partners, and can change over time (more on this in a moment).

T-Mobile also has its own Picks services. T-Satellite can be activated with one Pick, and so can the company’s new Optimized Video Calling service, which gives video calls a higher data priority for better quality.

If you’re looking to buy a new phone, you could get one for between one and three Picks depending on the device — in other words, you can forgo fancy add-on perks to get discounts on a new handset. Phone picks automatically inherit the Flex 36-month financing term.

To give Picks a real-world analogy, picture a restaurant buffet. You’re given a plate that’s sized based on how many Picks are available to your account. A Standard plan with one line would have the smallest plate (one Pick), while a Loaded plan with four lines would have a much larger plate (11 Picks).

The Picks on an account can be pooled depending on the group’s needs. A family of four on the Loaded plan, for example, might decide to get Netflix Premium to watch movies without ads (4 Picks), DashPass to save money on food deliveries (1 Pick), Xbox Game Pass Premium (2 Picks) and Pandora Plus (1 Pick) for entertainment and then a new phone for Mom (3 Picks).

The number of Picks you get depends on the plan and how many lines it includes. Not using a Pick doesn’t lower the plan price, and you’re not able to pay more for extra Picks (like adding a Verizon perk, for example) aside from moving to a more expensive plan.

Also, Picks are separate from the company’s perks such as T-Mobile Tuesdays promotions, discounts on hotels and rental cars, Delta premium in-flight drinks and MLB TV.

The next Picks component is timing. Every 90 calendar days, you can switch your Picks. Did you burn through all the shows you wanted to watch on Hulu? At the next Picks window, you can switch it for another option, or dump some 1- and 2-value Picks and pool them to get a new phone.

If you’re in the middle of the schedule and want to pick up Netflix to see what everyone is talking about in season four of The Diplomat, you can do that by canceling an existing Pick service and adding the streaming service for a fee, which Samson said would be in the $10 to $15 range. Or, at any time you can move up to a plan with more Picks (such as from More to Loaded).

The exceptions to that timing are T-Mobile’s Picks; you could turn on T-Satellite if you know you’re going remote backpacking, as long as a Pick is available in your plan.

#3036. Nvidia Fell While AMD and Broadcom Jumped. Here’s What History Says Happens Next to All 3 Stocks.

The news that led Jensen Huang to step down as CEO of Nvidia has crushed the company's stock price.

Nvidia (NVDA -2.01%) shareholders have had a rough few weeks. Nvidia's stock was a bit weak heading into November amid a marketwide AI sell-off, but in the days since news broke that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, the stock has taken a beating. That weakness has continued after Huang’s announcement on Thursday that he was stepping down from the CEO role. CFO Colette Kress has been tapped to lead the company on an interim basis while the board searches for the next CEO.

Some companies' losses are others' gains, and while Nvidia is down 21% so far this month, AMD (AMD -8.75%) has risen by around 4% and Broadcom (AVGO -4.76%) is up about 6%. That's a major mismatch, but the question is: What happens next with this trio of chipmakers?

Let's take a look at what history has to say about what's going on, and consider which stock may be the best to buy of this trio right now.

These three companies are all competitors in the data center computing world. Nvidia and AMD design GPUs, which are broad-purpose computing units that excel at handling a wide range of computationally heavy workloads. However, that flexibility comes at a cost. GPUs are more expensive to manufacture, buy, and operate than chips that are purpose-built for narrow types of AI workloads. That's where Broadcom's application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) come in — those custom AI chips are becoming quite popular with data center operators.

Nvidia has by far the largest data center segment of the three. During its most recently reported quarter, its data center revenue rose 117% year over year to $89 billion. Broadcom's AI semiconductor division is far smaller, with quarterly revenue of $16.7 billion. However, it was growing at a much faster 221% year-over-year pace.

AMD is in last place among the three. Its data center revenues grew at a "slower" 97% year-over-year pace to $8.5 billion.

However, if Nvidia's market leadership slips, AMD would likely have the most to gain. Broadcom's chips are becoming increasingly popular, but they can't do everything a GPU can.

Huang has resigned, and the question now is: How well can Nvidia survive without him? While he was deeply involved in the details of the operation and the loss of his leadership will be a blow to the company, there are likely numerous people who could succeed him and keep Nvidia on track. Companies go through CEO transitions all the time without getting derailed — even when (as in this case) there’s no clear succession plan in place.

I think that will be the case for Nvidia, and I'm not worried, as I think its products speak for themselves.

With that in mind, where could these three stocks go from here?

I think the best way to value these stocks is to look at their prices relative to next year's earnings projections. Starting with Broadcom, it's already in fiscal year 2027, and it trades at 17 times forward earnings.

Between Nvidia and AMD, there is a huge mismatch. Nvidia's stock hasn't gotten much respect over 2026, while AMD's valuation has soared. After the latest sell-off, Nvidia trades at just 10.6 times next year's earnings. Meanwhile, AMD trades for three times as much at 29 times next year's earnings.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

The question is, what is a reasonable price to pay for these companies?

I think AMD's valuation is far too high, and that could sap its future returns. Nvidia's is dirt cheap and ripe for a strong rebound once this news cycle blows over, but I can understand why some investors want to steer clear for a while.

Lastly, Broadcom has no problems and is trading at a cheap level. If you're looking for the AI chipmaker with the highest upside and the lowest risk, I think Broadcom is the clear winner here.
